chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about faeces falling into the well. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Draw out ten buckets from it. But if it has melted/dissolved, then forty or fifty buckets.'
ai.seo_question: How many buckets of water must be removed from a well if feces fall into it according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'qillah' (small quantity) water purity by defining the specific volume of water displaced by impurities, distinguishing between solid feces requiring ten buckets and dissolved feces requiring forty to fifty. It reflects the Shia juristic methodology of linking physical contamination levels to ritual purification standards, ensuring that the water remains fit for use after the removal of the affected portion. This ruling is foundational in fiqh al-taharah for determining when a well's water is considered pure after removing the impurity.
